WRMI = (waterlevelpercent) × (waterqualityindex / 100) × (1 − wastetanklevelpercent / 100)

So please use this multiplicative formula rather than the additive average you proposed. The "Water Conservation Requirement" corresponds to systems where this WRMI value is below 0.5.

args.sql:
SELECT l.stationname, l.locationtype, w.waterlevelpercent, w.waterqualityindex, w.wastetanklevelpercent,
  w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0) AS wrmi
FROM location l JOIN waterandwaste w ON l.loceqref = w.watereqref
LIMIT 5;

SELECT l.stationname, l.locationtype,
  AVG(w.waterqualityindex) AS avg_wqi,
  AVG(w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0)) AS avg_wrmi,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0) < 0.5) AS systems_needing_conservation
FROM location l JOIN waterandwaste w ON l.loceqref = w.watereqref
GROUP BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
ORDER BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
LIMIT 10;

SELECT stationname, locationtype, avg_wqi, avg_wrmi, systems_needing_conservation,
  CASE WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
       WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
       ELSE 'Sustainable Management' END AS classification,
  CASE WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Water Conservation Required'
       ELSE 'No Conservation Required' END AS management_situation
FROM (
  SELECT l.stationname, l.locationtype,
    AVG(w.waterqualityindex) AS avg_wqi,
    AVG(w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0)) AS avg_wrmi,

  FROM location l JOIN waterandwaste w ON l.loceqref = w.watereqref
  GROUP BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
) sub
ORDER BY stationname, locationtype
LIMIT 5;

tool_trajectory.result:
The WRMI is not computed as a simple average of the three normalized components. Instead, it is defined as a multiplicative composite:

WRMI = (waterlevelpercent) × (waterqualityindex / 100) × (1 − wastetanklevelpercent / 100)

SELECT l.stationname, l.locationtype, w.waterlevelpercent, w.waterqualityindex, w.wastetanklevelpercent,
  w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0) AS wrmi
FROM location l JOIN waterandwaste w ON l.loceqref = w.watereqref
LIMIT 5;

SELECT l.stationname, l.locationtype,
  AVG(w.waterqualityindex) AS avg_wqi,
  AVG(w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0)) AS avg_wrmi,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.waterlevelpercent * (w.waterqualityindex/100.0) * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent/100.0) < 0.5) AS systems_needing_conservation
FROM location l JOIN waterandwaste w ON l.loceqref = w.watereqref
GROUP BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
ORDER BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
LIMIT 10;

SELECT stationname, locationtype, avg_wqi, avg_wrmi, systems_needing_conservation,
  CASE WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
       WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
       ELSE 'Sustainable Management' END AS classification,
  CASE WHEN avg_wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Water Conservation Required'
       ELSE 'No Conservation Required' END AS management_situation
FROM (

tool_trajectory.result:
The WRMI is not computed as a simple average of the three normalized components. Instead, it is defined as a multiplicative composite:

WRMI = (waterlevelpercent) × (waterqualityindex / 100) × (1 − wastetanklevelpercent / 100)
